findings.title: Dynamic code or shell execution
findings.impact: If any input reaches these calls, an attacker can execute arbitrary code or commands.
findings.whyItMatters: Injection (OWASP A03) frequently starts at eval/exec style sinks.
findings.fix: Replace with a safe API (argument arrays, parsers, allowlists). Never build commands or code from strings that include external input.
findings.verification: Trace data flow into each call; add a unit test with hostile input.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: No eval/Function/shell-string execution remains, or each remaining use is documented with a proven constant input.
findings.caveats: Pattern match only. The call may only receive constants; confirm by data-flow review.

findings.title: SQL built by string concatenation or interpolation

evidence.excerpt: const rows = await db.query(`SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ${id}`);

findings.impact: Possible SQL injection and unpredictable query plans.
findings.whyItMatters: Parameterized queries are the primary defence against injection (OWASP A03).
findings.fix: Use parameterized queries or the ORM query builder. Allowlist any dynamic identifiers.
findings.verification: Search for the pattern again; add an injection test (e.g. a quote character in input).
findings.acceptanceCriteria: All queries with external input use bind parameters.
findings.caveats: Heuristic. Interpolated values may be constants or already validated.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled

evidence.excerpt: export const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false });

findings.impact: Connections can be intercepted by a man-in-the-middle.
findings.whyItMatters: Disabled verification removes the authenticity guarantee of TLS.
findings.fix: Enable verification. For private CAs, trust the CA bundle explicitly instead of disabling checks.
findings.verification: Connect to a host with an invalid cert and confirm the call fails.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: No production code path disables certificate verification.
findings.caveats: May be limited to a local dev profile; confirm it cannot reach production.

findings.title: Circular dependency between modules (src/api <-> src/db)
findings.impact: Cyclic modules cannot be understood, tested, versioned or deployed independently.
findings.whyItMatters: Acyclic dependencies keep change local and make extraction (e.g. to a service) feasible.
findings.fix: Extract the shared concept into a lower-level module or invert one dependency behind an interface.
findings.verification: Re-run `archsutra map`; cycles list must be empty. Add the check to CI.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: archsutra map reports zero module cycles.
findings.caveats: Module = top-level directory heuristic; a cycle between sub-folders of one deliberate unit may be acceptable.

findings.title: Lower layer depends on a higher layer
findings.impact: Data or service code that imports presentation code inverts the intended dependency direction and blocks reuse.
findings.whyItMatters: Layer direction is what keeps business and data logic independent of delivery mechanisms.
findings.fix: Move shared types down, or introduce an interface owned by the lower layer and implemented above.
findings.verification: Add a dependency-direction fitness test (e.g. dependency-cruiser, ArchUnit) and run it in CI.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: No import from data/service layers into presentation layers.
findings.caveats: Layers are inferred from folder names (controllers, services, repositories...). Verify your real layering.

findings.title: No CI pipeline configuration found

evidence.excerpt: No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines, Jenkins or CircleCI files found

findings.impact: Regressions and architecture drift are not caught automatically.
findings.whyItMatters: Automated gates are the cheapest enforcement of architectural rules.
findings.fix: Add CI that builds, tests, lints and runs dependency/secret scans on every pull request.
findings.verification: Open a PR and confirm the pipeline runs.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: A required status check runs build + tests on every PR.
findings.caveats: CI may live outside this repository.

findings.title: No test files found

evidence.excerpt: No test/, tests/, __tests__, *.test.*, *.spec.* or *_test.* files found

findings.impact: Refactoring and modernization are high-risk without a safety net.
findings.whyItMatters: Tests are the precondition for safe evolution.
findings.fix: Add characterization tests around critical paths before changing them.
findings.verification: Run the suite in CI and track coverage trend.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Critical user journeys have automated tests that run in CI.
findings.caveats: Tests may live in another repository.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.impact: A compromised process has root inside the container, easing escape and file tampering.
findings.fix: Create an unprivileged user and add `USER <name>` before the entrypoint.
findings.verification: `docker run --rm image id` shows a non-zero uid.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Final image stage runs as a non-root user.
findings.caveats: Some build-only stages legitimately use root; only the final stage matters.

findings.title: Dependency manifest without lockfile

evidence.excerpt: no lockfile next to or above this package.json

findings.impact: Installs are not reproducible; a compromised new release can enter automatically.
findings.whyItMatters: Lockfiles pin the exact dependency tree that was tested.
findings.fix: Commit the lockfile and install with `npm ci` (or equivalent) in CI.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: Every manifest has a committed lockfile.
findings.caveats: Workspaces may keep a single lockfile at the repo root (checked).

findings.title: Unpinned dependency ranges ("latest" or "*")
findings.impact: Any future release, including a malicious one, is accepted.
findings.whyItMatters: Unbounded ranges defeat review and reproducibility.
findings.fix: Use a bounded semver range and rely on the lockfile plus automated update PRs.

findings.title: No README at repository root
findings.impact: New contributors cannot find purpose, setup, or architecture overview.
findings.whyItMatters: Docs drift starts when the entry point is missing.
findings.fix: Add a README with purpose, setup, run, test, and an architecture section.
findings.verification: A new developer runs the project from the README alone.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: README exists and setup steps were validated on a clean machine.

findings.title: Container base image not pinned

evidence.excerpt: base image not pinned to a version or digest

findings.impact: Builds are not reproducible and can silently pick up a compromised or breaking image.
findings.whyItMatters: Pinning is a core supply-chain control.
findings.fix: Pin to a specific version tag, ideally with a digest, and update via automated PRs.
findings.verification: Rebuild twice and compare image digests.
findings.acceptanceCriteria: All FROM lines specify an explicit version or digest.
findings.caveats: Multi-stage references to earlier stages are not images.
